## Where can agents be used in infectious disease modelling?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Many of the tasks often given to early career researchers
- Reading data. Pulling numbers out of reports, tables and figures
- Building the infrastructure. Checks that rerun whenever the model or
  data change
- Talking through model development. A rubber duck that answers back
- How much agents should do on their own is an open question
- Most tasks still need a person closely in the loop
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](figures/agents-workflow-agents.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="The six-step workflow, question, data, model, fit, check and
report, with a tag over each. People over question; agents read and
digitise over data; people choose, agents write over model; agents,
every push over fit; agents run, people judge over check; agents draft,
people sign over report."}

fig-alt="A yellow rubber duck sitting beside a computer keyboard."}

## Implementing, optimising and reviewing

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- **Implementation.** From a spec or a conversation, to tasks, to code
- **Optimisation.** Custom gradients that make fitting faster
- **Theory.** Analytical solutions where we had used numerical ones
- **Review.** Review agents before we read the code
- Our time goes on review
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](figures/agents-agent-2.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="A spec or a conversation leads to agents writing the tasks,
which feed a loop of read, write, run and check. Passing code becomes a
pull request, which review agents send back into the loop and we review.
Merging refits the model and raises new tasks."}

::: {.attribution}

and [#902](https://github.com/epiforecasts/BVDOutbreakSize/pull/902), 2026 ·

primarycensored [#334](https://github.com/epinowcast/primarycensored/pull/334), 2026

## Google's tree search topped the CDC forecast hubs

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- An LLM-guided tree search that writes forecasting code
- First in the CDC FluSight hub, 2025/26
- Many prompts are drawn from models already in the hubs
- Bracher and Funk found the gain Aygün et al. claimed in retrospect came
  from data revisions leaking into the evaluation
- 207,500 candidate models
- My guess is few groups have that compute
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](figures/agents-martinson2026-fig2.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Inputs of a problem statement, data, libraries and evaluation
requirements feed a tree of candidate models, each node coloured by its
score, with the best leaf circled and the forecasting code it produced,
an SIR model fitted with scipy, shown as the output."}
